citation_title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models

primary_verification.abstract: Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions and guides current-task actor learning, while prior behavior is preserved by distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes. Fixed visual features keep the inherited learner and its replay compatible with base-policy updates. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and significantly reduces real-robot training time by 31.0\% to 68.5\%.

### E-M2 — AXIS-Bench：质量定义、标签粒度与微调方式需要一起比较

- Source ID：`arxiv:2610.18869v1`；类型：paper / model-learning evaluation；来源：[abs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18869v1)、[方法正文](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.18869v1)、[项目](https://axis-bench.github.io/)。
- 标题：*What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study*；作者：Mingxuan Yan、Litian Gong、Dihong Huang、Zhixu Li、Tianyu Zhang、Wenqian Zhang、Hefeifei Jiang、Peihao Li、Jian Zhang、Mengfei Zhao、Yikai Tang、Hai Zhai、Zehao Wang、Ruijian Liang、Yanjia Huang、Lin Shao、Changliu Liu、Kaiyu Hang、Zhiwen Fan、Masayoshi Tomizuka、Jianfei Yang、Jiachen Li。原始 HTML 三类 citation metadata 完整核验；`citation_date=2026/10/13`；v1 `2026-10-13 17:59:52 UTC`。
- First seen：2026-10-14；scan window：上述窗口；Impact：High；Decision：**Read**；Learning track：Embodied / Training；Signal type：model；Status：NEW。
- Target question：同样的次优示范，是过滤、加权还是条件学习更合适？episode/chunk 质量标签如何与目标任务微调协议相互作用？
- Evidence：§3–5 基于可 replay 的模拟 demonstrations，保留物体和 contact state 以重算质量标签；§4 以接近物体与接触后进展构造 approach-aware reward，再生成 chunk/episode 标签，对比 weighting/filtering/conditioning；每个 VLA 内对齐数据和训练预算。§5.1 比较 π0.5、SmolVLA、X-VLA，但各自初始化与可训练模块不同。§5.4 固定质量 tag 的微调也要测试带/不带 tag 的推理，tag 本身不是通用增益开关。
- 模型/学习价值：数据“质量”不是一个脱离目标的分数；质量定义、粒度、训练使用方式及微调输入契约共同决定收益。conditioning 平均偏向 episode、filtering 平均偏向 chunk，论文同时报告反例。
- 系统影响（推断）：可 replay 数据需保留 state/contact 与相机配置；质量标签生成与动作监督窗口要版本化，避免离线打分与在线样本不同步。
- 关键数字防误读：论文的真实任务 `9.6% → 31.7%` 是**普通 BC 模拟预训练相对无预训练**的收益，不是质量 conditioning 的收益；conditioning 为 `32.5%`，仅比 plain BC 高 `0.83 percentage points`，十项任务中五升四降一平（§6.2）。这些是作者数据，不是本地复现。
- 边界：共享 tabletop simulation；真实评估仅一种 VLA、一个参考 workspace。进展标签可能低估准备/恢复动作；跨模型比较不能分离初始化原因。项目页明确 **Code (Coming Soon)、Dataset (Coming Soon)**，不能宣称已可复现。
- Reason：方法控制和反例能改变“过滤低分轨迹就一定更好”的工程判断；无代码不抹掉已披露学习机制。
- Related topics：具身数据配方、动作 chunk、训练分布与评估；Next：与已读质量/混采框架对照，先定义自己的 label/selection/FT/inference 对照矩阵；共享 P1 候选，保持 NEW。

citation_title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study

primary_verification.abstract: Abstract: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Within each VLA, we match demonstrations and training budgets. Additional comparisons examine pretraining data size and the roles of quality tags during fine-tuning and inference. Across three VLAs, we find that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning; conditioning and filtering favor episode and chunk labels, respectively, on average, with model-dependent reversals; and constant-tag fine-tuning improves mean success after conditioned pretraining with either tagged or untagged inference. We introduce AXIS-Bench to support these controlled comparisons. Built on crowdsourced simulation demonstrations, it provides recorded object and contact states for recomputing quality labels on shared trajectories. Replayable trajectories support workspace-aligned rendering and user-defined real-world target tasks. In our real-world experiment, simulation pretraining raises success from 9.6\% to 31.7\%. Project page: this https URL .

- Target question：网络推理期间动作已被执行、指令被切换或队列耗尽，如何防止旧结果恢复已经失效的机器人动作？
- Evidence：PR 完整 146 文件列表已取两页；重点读 `inference/execution.py`、`remote_inference/client.py`、`engine.py`、`chunk_contract.py` 及相关回归差异。prediction/执行分离，robot 端持有队列与 motor 权限；observation age、request identity、execution generation、committed cursor 绑定 chunk，迟到结果不能重新授权旧动作。耗尽后要求本地 hold acknowledgment 和 fresh capture 才恢复，deadline 不因反复检查续期。
- 测试证据：存在 `test_reset_and_timeout_make_late_results_ineligible`、`test_replace_future_requires_current_cursor_and_generation`、`test_starvation_requires_hold_ack_and_fresh_capture_before_recovery`、remote/local parity、session ownership 和 shutdown 测试。作者报告 540 passed / 4 skipped；本次 head SHA 的公开 Full Tests / GPU Tests 等为 success（保存 check-runs），没有本地运行。
- Reason：改变真实部署执行语义，且可以沿代码和回归核验，不是只添加远程 API。
- 边界：一 server/checkpoint、一 active client；自动重连、并发多 client、history-dependent policies 不在实现范围；远端 hosted GPU、routed 硬件与 trained RTC 真机验收仍为作者待办。驱动必须声明 position-hold 支持。旧 async 命令被替换，Unitree G1/SONIC 暂无支持的 remote replacement。
- 历史区别：#4836 于 10-12 合并后被 #4936 撤回，昨天已记录；**#4937 是 10-13 的重新引入事件**。不可继续写成“当前无 remote inference”，也不可重复算 #4836。

observed.title: Trust-Calibrated VLA Policy Post-Training with Evolving Imagination

citation_title: Trust-Calibrated VLA Policy Post-Training with Evolving Imagination

primary_verification.abstract: Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are often pretrained via imitation learning, making reinforcement learning (RL) post-training important when deployment moves beyond demonstration coverage. Existing refinement paradigms expose a reliability--efficiency tension: model-free refinement avoids simulator bias but is interaction-intensive, whereas model-based refinement can exploit unreliable imagination even as its simulator adapts. We propose Model-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (MERL), a trust-calibrated framework that couples policy optimization with an online-updated simulator comprising a world model and a reward proxy head. Across stages, simulator reliability controls the imagined-data ratio and rollout horizon; within rollouts, chunk-level trust controls replay selection and optimization weight. For recursive imagination without exact grounded continuations, a residual predictor estimates trust without querying future ground truth. On perturbed LIBERO-PRO tasks, MERL reaches 79.7% average success, improves high-threshold learning speed by 10.9% over the matched model-free control, and outperforms same-protocol external baselines across three training seeds. Fixed-data adaptation from 50 demonstrations per task achieves 80.0% average success on two physical-robot tasks.

observed.title: Value-Preserving Action Quantization

primary_verification.abstract: Abstract: Search-based policy learning, such as Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), offers the flexibility to trade runtime computation for data efficiency and adaptation to novel environments. For robot learning, however, applying search requires discretizing the continuous action space and associated dynamics, typically through action quantization. While reconstruction-based quantization is sufficient for representing the continuous action space alone, policy learning additionally requires the quantized actions to preserve their effects on future states and values. We show that such requirement is not necessarily captured by action reconstruction error. Instead, we prove that the error in the value function resulting from action quantization is tightly bounded by the reconstruction error of state reachability under the quantized actions. Based on these results, we propose value-preserving action quantization (VAQ), which quantizes actions by preserving state reachability. We further combine VAQ with MCTS (VAQ-MCTS) as a value-preserving, search-based policy learning framework for behavioral cloning. Using a wide range of object pushing tasks as a controlled benchmark, we evaluate VAQ-MCTS against state-of-the-art behavioral cloning methods. VAQ-MCTS matches or exceeds their performance under standard settings, while substantially improving data efficiency and robustness to heterogeneous demonstrations, while enabling zero-shot adaptation to novel environments. Hardware experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of VAQ-MCTS, completing all 30 real-world object pushing trials with only 10 minutes of demonstration data.
